verdict: THE CENSUS DOES NOT GIVE CAUSATION — STRUCTURE-ALONE IS NULL EVEN NEAR-FIELD. The one positive number (whole-field Spearman +0.020, biosim's) is just the DISTANCE ENVELOPE — 'closer to the removed piece = more affected, on average' — which is trivially true and does NOT tell you the effect. The moment you ask the real question — WITHIN the immediate neighbourhood, which pieces actually fire? — structure propagation is at chance (1-hop lift -0.022, 2-hop -0.050, 3-hop -0.101). The structure-only cause screen is likewise near-chance. So: the MAP (who exists, who neighbours whom) is done, but it CANNOT compute a removal's effect — only that a coherent module exists there (biosim's blast radius, real for tight complexes, coarse). Genuine remove-and-calculate lives ENTIRELY in the intervention data: for the ~2,000 pieces measured (Perturb-seq) the effect is known, and the engines that work (whodunit/diagnose) stand on that MEASURED fingerprint, not on the census. The bottleneck to 'remove ANY piece and calculate its effect' is therefore SURVEILLANCE — measured interventions across more pieces and conditions — not more census. This is the sharpest form of the structure-vs-dynamics split the whole project keeps hitting.
